name: Sampler
description: Sample player with 16 pads, waveform editing, kit management
changelog: 0.16.0: a kit loads only as far as its pads play. Each reloaded pad is asked whether the engine can sound it (SamplerAudioCallbacks::padPlayable): a pad the kit gives no sample goes dark, one whose sample did not load dim red, and only a pad that plays takes its colour -- the panel taking the new kit's pads mid-swap no longer paints every pad loaded at once. KIT LOADED counts playable pads of those with a sample; a kit none of whose pads plays is a failed load with the reason on the loader bar (no samples on pads / no sample loaded), current so the pad editor can fill it. The waveform cache is read back with the largest buffer PSRAM has (256 kB down to 16), where a fixed 256 kB malloc failed after a few kit changes and every waveform was computed again off the card under the streamer. Swap log: empty=, failed=, why=.

0.15.0: a kit whose samples are not at the engine's rate (48 kHz on the 44.1 kHz engine costs every voice an interpolation: ~53 us a voice against ~10) is offered, once after it loads, Convert / Not now / Never (keep_rate in the kit). Convert runs core's KitRateConverter on a worker with a progress dialog and Stop; the kit is reloaded at the new rate and the originals nothing names any more are removed (retried while a voice still reads one, finished when the kit is loaded again). An offer goes when its kit does. Together with 0.14.0's direct hit path. Requires core 1.68.0.

0.14.0: a finger's hit goes straight into the engine on the thread that read it (player.playPad), first of everything a hit does -- no event queue, no task on the render's core between the STM's note and the voice; the take's playback and MIDI notes keep the event. A touch the STM reports before its velocity (core onPadTouch, PAD_TOUCH) arms the note the hit will play (player.armPad); the hit only sets its level, a touch that leaves drops it (player.disarmPad). Requires core 1.67.0.

0.13.0: the level meter beside the waveform in Arrange's look -- a dark well, two columns of segments, green to -6 dB, amber to -1, red above, unlit at a fifth; up at once, down ~28 dB a second -- and as tall as the waveform's panel, level with it (it ran the height of the pad grid). Reads the loudest since its last 50 ms tick, so a hit between two is shown. Requires crosspad-gui 1.26.0 (create_segment_meter).

0.12.0: main's Sampler 0.8.2-0.8.4 merged in -- a quiet kit swap starts at once, the waveform loader no longer stays LOADING, a hold-mode release cuts the voice before the MIDI echo, the pitched editor's Voices up to the voice cap, the kit selector stops at its last kit instead of wrapping, waveform cache entries relative to the kit's folder, kit_load_task_is_worker(). The pad editor keeps 0.11.0's turned control.

0.11.0: A control being turned in the pad editor stays the one being turned when another pad is struck -- PITCH, VOL, PAN, HP, LP, CHOKE, the colour, START and END (in FINE the picture zooms in round the new pad's marker) -- so pad after pad is tuned without reaching for it again; nothing turned, nothing is. START and END in FINE speed up when turned fast: detents one way under 120 ms apart double the step, 1 ms up to 64 ms a detent; a pause or a turn back is 1 ms again.

0.10.0: NORM in the pad editor brings a pad's sample up until its loudest moment sits at -0.3 dB, as a copy beside it (<name>_norm.wav) the pad then plays -- trim, pitch and filters stay, the original is not touched, a sample already at full level is left alone. PLAY and LOOP are their symbols alone to make room. Needs core 1.56.

0.9.0: a take keeps what each hit sounded as. Under 16 levels a hit is recorded as the source pad at its level -- velocity or pitch -- with the velocity Full level or the ramp made of it, and plays back that way with the mode off; a plain part plays its own pads with the mode on. The modes shape what a finger plays, not a take's playback. The pad logic offers its 16 levels to other apps (core IPadPerformance), so the Sequencer can turn it on. Needs core 1.55.

0.8.4: a hold-mode release cuts the voice before the MIDI echo goes out (a host that reads USB MIDI slowly no longer holds the cut back); the waveform loader is marked running before its task is created, so a waveform no longer stays LOADING; a setting being turned in the pad editor stays turned on the next pad; requires core 1.45.0, the first core on main with PitchedInstrument::voiceCap() (0.8.3's 1.43.0 was the firmware line's release/core-1.43.0)
0.8.3: the pitched editor's Voices goes up to the board's voice cap (PitchedInstrument::voiceCap(), which every setParams now meets); requires core 1.43.0
0.8.2: a kit swap with no pad sounding starts on the first pad at once instead of 150 ms later (the wait stays while a pad sounds)
0.8.1: + NEW finds a free kit name with stat(), and a name the card cannot answer for counts as taken ("card read failed"); no <fstream> left (smaller firmware image)

0.8.0: the Unsaved changes dialog in the look of the rest of the device -- Save, Discard (red), Cancel, the pads changed, the encoder on Save, the power button backs out of it; requires crosspad-gui 1.16

0.7.0: the Sampler's screen in the device's design, as the Recorder and the pad editor wear it -- dark, flat buttons, the accent on what is on: back, the pad last hit (in its colour) and the kit (opens the browser) along the top; the pads in the kit's colours, faint at rest, full while they sound, the last one outlined; the sample's file and view (FILE, live scope) over the waveform, the time under it, the meter beside; FULL LEVEL, 16 LEVELS, EDIT along the bottom. The waveform in the pad editor's colours (a lit field, the part outside the trim greyed, start teal, end red, the playhead white), in the pitched editor too

0.6.0: what the pad editor does in the background shows on the waveform, where it is looked at: PROCESSING with the percentage and which of PITCH, HP, LP, REV the copy carries, or LOADING and the file, one line and a thin bar at the top, the dots moving while the card is waited on; the line under the waveform no longer says it

0.5.0: the pad editor laid out as the Recorder is -- the pad in its colour (turned: the colour), its sample, REV, the mode, COPY; VOL, PAN, PITCH, HP, LP, CHOKE; the sample drawn with the trim lit; START/END turned column then millisecond with a zoom; PLAY, LOOP (with a playhead), FULL, DEL. REV (backwards, and drawn so -- mirrored in the editor and the panel, START on the left over the sample's end, turned the way it is heard), PITCH -12..+12 semitones (varispeed), HP and LP 12 dB/octave filters in thirds of an octave: the player can do none of it, so such a pad plays a copy rendered once in .fx/ beside its sample (by the editor when the values settle, by the kit load task when one is missing); kit.json keeps pitch, hp, lp, reverse. The colour is saved now, and a new or removed sample asks to be saved; requires core 1.31; a value being turned reads dark on the accent: the text colour sits on the button, which is the only thing ever EDITED, not on its label

0.4.0: the kit browser in two lists, LEGACY (the kits a board ships with) and USER (made on it: KitInfo::isUser(), the Slicer's), switched on the status bar; it opens on the list the loaded kit is in; requires core 1.29
0.2.1: Fix pad editor file browser off-screen, params panel scroll, pad-editor playback silence, live start/end trim preview
0.2.0: Wire SamplerPadLogic, EventBus audio bridge, kit load task, end=0 normalization
0.1.0: Initial release — pad playback, waveform view, kit selector
